html:
Northern Cyprus is the northern third of the island of Cyprus, held by Turkish Cypriots with Turkish troops since 1974. Only Turkey recognises it as a state.

Cyprus became independent from Britain in 1960 with a shared government of Greek and Turkish Cypriots. It broke down in fighting in 1963 and 1964, and Turkish Cypriots withdrew into enclaves. In July 1974 the military junta in Athens backed a coup against President Makarios, aiming to join the island to Greece. Turkey answered with the invasion of Cyprus and took the north. Well over 150,000 Greek Cypriots fled south and tens of thousands of Turkish Cypriots moved north.

A ceasefire line patrolled by the United Nations has divided the island since. The north declared itself the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus in 1983. In 2004 Turkish Cypriots voted for the Annan Plan to reunite the island and Greek Cypriots voted against it, so only the south joined the European Union.
sum: Northern Cyprus is the northern third of the island of Cyprus, held by Turkish Cypriots with Turkish troops since 1974. Only Turkey recognises it as a state.
